status: PROPOSED - NOT CANONICAL - research fixture for WP-B1; owner scientific-method approval pending
generated_by: Claude, WP-B1, 2026-10-28; values transcribed from USNO API responses; nothing computed by the Sabpuja engine, Swiss Ephemeris or PR #48
important: These are ASTRONOMICAL (upper-limb, refracted) sunrise/sunset times for the exact coordinates shown. They are not Hindu (centre, no refraction) sunrise times, not Rashtriya Panchang values, and not valid for any other point in the same city.

location.label: Delhi reference point
location.elevation_m: not an input; USNO assumes sea level, level unobstructed horizon
location.coordinate_note: Reference coordinates chosen for this fixture and sent to USNO exactly as shown. Not a DATA-01 gazetteer entry and not asserted to equal the prototype's curated places.

cases.utc_offset_source: fixed offset passed to USNO as tz parameter; dst=false
cases.convention: USNO astronomical: upper limb on a level sea horizon; centre geometrically 50 arcmin below horizontal (16' mean semidiameter + 34' mean refraction); geocentric-to-topocentric handling per USNO, not stated in detail
cases.precision: 1 minute in local time; USNO states computed rise/set times may be in error by a minute or more because refraction is unpredictable

proposed_tolerance.rule: |engine - published| <= 120 s for sunrise and sunset
proposed_tolerance.justification: 60 s for minute publication with unstated rounding, plus up to 60 s for differences in refraction model (fixed 34' at USNO versus Swiss pressure/temperature model) and solar semidiameter. Proposed only.

cases.use_under_option_SUN_B: Not a direct reference. Usable only as a differential anchor: the Hindu-rising time must exceed the published astronomical time by the geometric time for the Sun's centre to climb a further ~50' (independently computed in WP-B2 by a spherical-astronomy oracle). That check is DERIVED, not published.

location.label: High-latitude reference point inside the SCI-01g band
location.coordinate_note: Synthetic reference coordinates; 65.9 deg is inside the canonical +/-66.0 deg supported band

sundata.phen: Object continuously above the Twilight Limit

expected.option_SUN_A: No sunrise and no sunset on this date (published). Engine must return the typed code PANCHANGA_SUNRISE_UNDEFINED, never a guessed time: whole-object refusal under PAN-D11-A, or typed unavailable sunrise-dependent fields under the proposed PAN-D11-B (PAN-D11 PENDING).
expected.option_SUN_B: DERIVED, not published: the Sun's centre should still dip below the geometric horizon (needs |lat| < 90 - 23.44 = 66.56 deg at solstice), so a Hindu rising/setting is expected to exist. To be confirmed by the WP-B2 oracle; Swiss uses its slower algorithm here because |lat| > 65 deg for the Sun.

cases.why_selected: Shows that inside the canonical latitude band an astronomical-sunrise convention can be undefined while a centre/no-refraction convention is defined. Proves fail-closed handling is reachable in-band under SUN-A.

location.label: Tromso reference point (outside the SCI-01g band)

expected.sabpuja: Refused earlier by LATITUDE_OUTSIDE_SUPPORTED_BAND (canonical SCI-01g, |lat| > 66.0). Panchanga must not reach sunrise computation. The published polar-night result documents why the band matters.
